prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / identity-preserve.
Asset type: heroic five-person cyberpunk CARTOON ensemble illustration for The ARC Daily Digest, based on our real MIT ARC group photo.
Image 1 is the group/composition and cybernetic costume reference. Image 2 is the original real group photograph and the absolute face/identity, left-to-right order and relative-height reference. Image 3 is the badge AESTHETIC reference ONLY: deep midnight navy/near-black, vivid luminous pink-magenta, stark ivory-white, large modular orthogonal puzzle shapes, fine checkerboard meshes, maze-like traces, stripes, pixel blocks and retro digital-grid rhythm. Ignore the badge's person's name and other wording; do not put that name on anyone. Image 4 is our established individual CARTOON STYLE reference (the open-helmet Dries avatar); apply that richly detailed, warmly characterized painterly 3D/comic treatment consistently to EVERY person and the entire setting.

Make a completely illustrated, exuberantly HEROIC CYBERPUNK team portrait. Five distinct smiling, recognizable research heroes together, head to boots visible, confident friendly stances, a slightly low cinematic camera, strong silhouettes and dynamic shoulder/arm poses, neither stiff passport lineup nor a battle scene. Preserve EXACTLY the five people from the original photograph, SAME LEFT-TO-RIGHT ORDER, identities, glasses, hairstyles and relative heights. The extreme-left man is especially TALL and long-limbed, not stocky. Transform faces into expressive polished cartoon likenesses; keep each actual face distinctive, warm and clearly visible. This is FULL CARTOON ART, no photographic faces, no photographic room or skin pasted into a drawing.

LEFT TO RIGHT:
1. Dries Smit, very tall, lean, brown swept hair, clean-shaven, big friendly smile. Inventive OPEN-FACED graphite/titanium skeletal helmet with green processor-fin crest and cyan/green light ribs, inspired by image 4. Both eyes visibly uncovered, only a tiny translucent green display beside the temple. Elaborate heroic GPU engineer exosuit, integrated shoulder/backpack fan hardware, illuminated cables, articulated gauntlets/boots, emerald accent in the common navy/pink palette.
2. Dark-haired puzzle master with slim rectangular glasses, slight facial stubble and friendly smile from original. One of TWO intentionally unnamed puzzle masters. A truly advanced navy/magenta/violet cybernetic suit with intricate neural headgear that leaves his face open, layered shoulder processors, fine checkerboard lattice circuit patterns, mechanical gauntlets, a spectacular floating pink geometric puzzle-grid construct above his hand. Clever magical-science hero, no magic wand or weapon.
3. Fair-haired puzzle master with glasses and warm smile from original. The other unnamed puzzle master. Equally ultra-advanced ivory/navy/gold-magenta open-faced neural crown and long technical mantle, elegant labyrinthine circuitry, multiple linked holographic puzzle planes and geometric tessellations floating around one hand. These TWO middle figures visibly have even more advanced, imaginative equipment than the rest.
4. Son Pham, East Asian man with black rectangular glasses, swept black hair and characteristic broad smile from original. Black/navy cyber-engineer hero suit with dense compact GPU headgear behind his glasses, brilliant blue/cyan cores within magenta-trimmed segmented armor, clever wrist projections and energetic stance. Keep his real facial likeness and shorter height relative to Dries and Matt.
5. Matt Mazur, tall, swept short dark hair, clean-shaven, distinctive friendly smile from original. Heroic charcoal/navy cybernetic suit, refined amber/cyan core accents within the shared pink/navy design, open-faced temple gear, sculpted shoulder/chest/forearm/leg equipment, relaxed confident testing-chief hero stance. Face unobscured.

BADGE THEME governs the WHOLE IMAGE, not a tiny prop: the five stand on a futuristic MIT research-lab/event platform in a grand navy interior whose original ribbed ceiling becomes receding circuit beams. Huge bright MAGENTA orthogonal modular puzzle shapes and tessellated blocks form architectural arches and panels behind the team. Checkerboard mesh, fine pink stripes, black-on-pink maze traces and ivory pixel-grid light tiles are integrated into panels, suit details and holograms. Deep navy background, saturated hot-pink rim lights, selective crisp ivory highlights, limited cyan/green/gold identity accents. The badge's graphic sensibility feels built into a richly drawn heroic world, not a rectangular photograph of a badge glued into the background.
Craftsmanship: crisp expressive linework, dimensional painterly cel shading, tactile metal and translucent holograms, dramatic perspective, rich contrast and luminous edges, fun sophisticated comic-book energy consistent with image 4. All five faces evenly readable, all five equally heroic, puzzle masters especially high-tech. Whole scene coherently cartoon, large readable forms plus intricate equipment detail. Wide LANDSCAPE group composition, roughly 4:3, with room around helmets and feet and good separation among five silhouettes.
No extra foreground characters, no animals, no anonymous added heroes, no duplicate people, no face-obscuring eyepatches/visors, no masks, no weapons, no fight scene, no logos, text, names, numbers, scores, headings, lettering, badges with writing, watermarks or copied badge name. This is a playful editorial illustration, not documentary hardware.

references.role: User-identified faces, left-to-right order and relative heights.
User-supplied navy, pink and ivory modular puzzle, maze and checkerboard aesthetic; printed name is not a cast instruction.
Established cartoon rendering style and open-faced Dries helmet design.

review: Visually inspected: exactly five recognizable smiling cartoon heroes in original order, tall Dries and open-faced helmet, advanced gear on the two middle puzzle masters, Son and Matt distinct, vivid badge-inspired navy/pink modular architecture and checkerboard details. No added names or scores. Mark approved this exact version for the X announcement.
editorApproval: User: Excellent and that one's good. That's the one we should post to Twitter.
